code_label: QCBM as near-term market generator
text_span: The quantum circuit Born machine (QCBM) is a generative quantum machine learning model that can be efficiently trained and run on the NISQ-era quantum processors.
rationale: States the paper’s central model and intended near-term applicability.

code_label: Financial data targets are heavy-tailed and spiky
text_span: In this paper we test QCBM performance on a dataset of spot FX log-returns (heavy-tailed distribution) as well as a specially constructed mixture of normal distributions
rationale: Identifies the two empirical distribution types used to evaluate the model.

code_label: Quantum expressive power claimed over RBM
text_span: The QCBM has greater expressive power than comparable classical neural networks such as the restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM)
rationale: Frames the comparative advantage claim motivating the study.

code_label: Non-differentiable GA training proposed
text_span: This paper proposes a non-differentiable learning approach to the training of the QCBM based on a genetic algorithm (GA).
rationale: Summarizes the main methodological contribution.

code_label: Training difficulty with non-smooth loss
text_span: The traditional differentiable learning approach may not work well when the loss function is highly non-smooth.
rationale: States a caveat motivating the alternative training method.

code_label: Generative models important across applications
text_span: Generative models form one of the most important classes of unsupervised machine learning techniques, with numerous applications
rationale: Provides the broader motivation for generative modeling.

code_label: GAN and RBM dominate prior applications
text_span: two neural network-based non-parametric learning approaches have gained widespread adoption in recent years: the generative adversarial network (GAN)
rationale: Positions the paper relative to established classical generative models.

code_label: Need for quantum advantage in NISQ era
text_span: there is a need to ﬁnd examples of quantum advantage – real-world applications of quantum computing that achieve results beyond the capabilities of classical computers.
rationale: States the broader research motivation.

code_label: QCBM described as quantum counterpart of RBM/GAN
text_span: Quantum generative models have all the necessary qualities to establish quantum advantage on NISQ devices.
rationale: Claims the model class is well suited to demonstrate advantage.

code_label: Single-run sampling advantage
text_span: generation of an independent sample from the learned distribution can be done in a single run of the quantum circuit in the case of the QCBM
rationale: Highlights a claimed sampling efficiency benefit.

code_label: RBM requires many passes to equilibrate
text_span: up to 103–104 forward and backward passes through the network in the case of the RBM
rationale: Contrasts QCBM sampling with RBM thermalization cost.

code_label: Non-differentiable methods suited to complex optimization
text_span: it may be more efficient to use the non-differentiable learning methods such as global optimization algorithms
rationale: Justifies the choice of GA and related methods.

code_label: GA chosen as learning algorithm of choice
text_span: In this paper we propose using GA as a non-differentiable learning algorithm of choice for training QCBMs.
rationale: Explicitly states the selected training approach.

code_label: QCBM architecture specified by layers and gates
text_span: To specify the QCBM architecture means to specify the number of layers, the type of adjustable gates, and the type of ﬁxed gates for each layer.
rationale: Defines the architectural design variables.

code_label: Two fixed entangling layers proposed
text_span: we suggest using two layers of ﬁxed 2-qubit gates sandwiched between layers of adjustable 1-qubit gates
rationale: Describes the chosen circuit structure.

code_label: Stronger entanglement expected from CX and CZ
text_span: Our initial guess is that CX (controlled bit-ﬂip) and CZ (controlled phase-ﬂip) should result in the strongest effects
rationale: States an architectural hypothesis about gate choice.

code_label: Twelve-qubit hardware-efficient circuit selected
text_span: Figure 1 displays a 12-qubit QCBM with two layers of controlled rotation gates
rationale: Specifies the concrete circuit size used in experiments.

code_label: Circuit depth chosen for NISQ feasibility
text_span: The circuit is wide enough and deep enough to learn a complex distribution of a continuous random variable while remaining implementable on the existing NISQ devices
rationale: Explains the design trade-off between expressivity and implementability.

code_label: Sequential connectivity requirement
text_span: The chosen QCBM architecture is compatible with the limited connectivity we observe in the current generation of quantum processors.
rationale: Notes hardware connectivity compatibility.

code_label: GA chromosome is a 12 by 7 angle matrix
text_span: The solution is a 12 × 7 matrix of rotation angles
rationale: Defines the GA representation of circuit parameters.

code_label: Mutation rate can decay over generations
text_span: The mutation rate can be either constant or time-dependent.
rationale: Describes a key hyperparameter choice.

code_label: Discrete angle search space defined
text_span: Rotation angles 𝜃j i are deﬁned on the interval −𝜋≤𝜃j i < 𝜋.
rationale: Specifies the parameter domain used by the GA.

code_label: Search space is enormous
text_span: For example, for m = 7 we have 128 possible values for each rotation angle, making the total number of possible conﬁgurations 12884 ≃ 10177.
rationale: Quantifies the combinatorial scale of the optimization problem.

code_label: Objective function based on sorted sample distances
text_span: The objective function F( ̂𝜃) can be deﬁned as follows: F( ̂𝜃) = K ∑ k=1 (uk − 𝑣k( ̂𝜃))2.
rationale: Defines the training loss used for GA optimization.

code_label: RBM architecture matched to QCBM parameter count
text_span: This network architecture makes the RBM equivalent to the QCBM described in Section 2 in the sense that both generative models have the same number of adjustable parameters
rationale: Explains the basis for the classical comparison model.

code_label: RBM sampling needs thermal equilibrium
text_span: In order to generate an independent sample it is necessary to achieve the state of thermal equilibrium where practically all information about the input is lost.
rationale: States a practical limitation of RBM sampling.

code_label: Contrastive divergence used for RBM training
text_span: the k-step contrastive divergence method [1,36,37] can be used to approximate 〈…〉model as shown in Algorithm 2.
locator: 3.1 Training RBM with contrastive divergence algorithm
rationale: Identifies the RBM training algorithm.

code_label: Binary encoding pipeline for real-valued data
text_span: we need to design a method of converting real-valued samples into binary features that can be taken by the network as an input for training
rationale: Describes the preprocessing required for both models.

code_label: Two datasets used for evaluation
text_span: We test the performance of the QCBM and RBM on two datasets.
rationale: States the empirical evaluation setup.

code_label: Dataset 1 is a spiky mixture of normals
text_span: A specially constructed distribution of a continuous random variable with a highly spiky probability density function (PDF) modeled as a mixture of normal distributions.
rationale: Describes the first benchmark dataset.

code_label: Dataset 2 is FX log returns
text_span: A heavy-tailed distribution of spot FX daily log-returns for the USD–JPY currency pair observed between 2001 and 2017
rationale: Describes the second benchmark dataset.

code_label: Generated samples visualized with PDF and QQ plots
text_span: This allows us to visualize the quality of the generated samples
rationale: Indicates the evaluation visualizations used.

code_label: Both models learn complex empirical distributions
text_span: We can see that both QCBM(12, 7) and RBM(12, 7) can successfully learn complex empirical distributions
rationale: Summarizes the main empirical finding from the plots.

code_label: CX chosen as fixed gate in experiments
text_span: We have chosen CX for the ﬁxed gates in QCBM and used the open-source Qiskit package
rationale: Specifies the gate choice and simulation tool.

code_label: GA hyperparameters set for exploration then exploitation
text_span: The best results were achieved for the CX ﬁxed gates and exponentially decreasing mutation rate
rationale: Reports the preferred hyperparameter pattern.

code_label: Mutation rate decays from 1.0 to 0.0625
text_span: the maximum value of the mutation rate is α = 1.0 and the minimum value is α = 0.0625
rationale: Quantifies the explored mutation schedule.

code_label: Finer angle discretization gives marginal gains
text_span: the GA performance improves only marginally for m > 5.
rationale: Reports the convergence observation about discretization granularity.

code_label: Two layers may be enough for deep QCBM
text_span: This means that for many practical purposes, it is sufficient to
rationale: Indicates a practical sufficiency threshold and implied design limit.

code_label: QCBM outperforms weakly tuned RBM on objective statistic
text_span: QCBM(12, 7) with a weakly optimized set of hyperparameters performs better than RBM(12, 7)
rationale: States the comparative performance conclusion.

code_label: Quantum advantage remains unproven
text_span: Although it cannot be seen as evidence of the quantum advantage
rationale: Explicitly cautions against overclaiming advantage.
